sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, at a 5.8% CAGR to $8.6 billion, lifting operating margin from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F19][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change in the top line, up 17.1% on rate cases, favorable weather and volumes, partly offset by an estimated impairment on the Commercial Renewables disposal groups [D239][P26].
FY2020 was the trough, with net income down 63.3% on coal ash settlement impairments and pandemic-driven volume losses [D157][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and 3.6pp of the 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest single driver, contributing 2.8pp on 6.6% growth and 43.3% of revenue [D776][D775][D774].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure added 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% and contributing 1.7pp [D566][D682][D683].
Operating costs grew 0.3pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at 5.3%, and incremental operating margin was 41.4% [D379][D372][D378].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% against 9.8% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 0.6% [D362][D360][D374].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, above the 22.9% median and the 19.7% low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
The margin rose 0.8pp in FY2025, while D&A climbed to 24.3% of revenue from 21.4% [D370][D341][D303].
In FY2025 net margin of 15.7% sat 11.5pp below the 27.2% operating margin, as interest expense of $3.6 billion and an 11.2% effective tax rate absorbed the gap [F47][F28][D967][X63][D345].
The margin expansion looks structural, built on rate-case recovery and a growing regulated asset base rather than cost cuts [P16][P25].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, below the 2.59x window median [F77][D346][D958].
Free cash flow was -$1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin, against a -5.8% window median [F97][D343][D939].
Capex of $14.0 billion was 44.2% of revenue and 1.82x D&A [F87][D342][D348].
FY2022 conversion fell to 20.7% of revenue as rising fuel costs created undercollections financed with borrowings [D224][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion in FY2025, net cash of -282.3% of revenue, against a -235.4% peer median [D352][D353][D969].
That ranks at the 33rd percentile of three peers, and the current ratio of 0.55x is the window low [D968][F177][D943].
Long-term debt rose 4.9% to $80.1 billion while equity grew 3.4% to $51.8 billion [D368][F187][D367][F197].
Dividends of $3.2 billion in FY2022 exceeded free cash flow, and the diluted share count rose 4.2% in FY2021 [D234][F94][D214].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025, below 1.0x, with current liabilities of $21.0 billion against current assets of $11.6 billion [R1][F177][F157][F147].
For a regulated utility this reflects heavy short-term debt maturities rather than a liquidity crisis, but it leaves little cushion [R1].
Net debt rose for nine straight years, from $50.0 billion in FY2016 to $89.6 billion in FY2025 [R3][D14][D352].
Debt-funded capex is the growth engine, so leverage will keep climbing unless rate base returns outpace borrowing [R3].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at -0.96x, 0.01x and -0.34x [R4][D269][D309][D347].
Persistent negative free cash flow means dividends and capex depend on continued capital-market access [R4].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 22.9% window median, in the FY2026 10-K [D933].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -282.3%, in the FY2026 10-K [D353].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers above the 2.59x window median, in the FY2026 10-K [D958].
